title: Cocks's hereditary treewidth–clique boundedness conjecture
statement: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a hereditary graph class. A graph $H$ is $H$-free in $\mathcal{G}$ when graphs in the relevant subclass have no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$. The class $\mathcal{G}$ is $(\operatorname{tw},\omega)$-bounded if there is a function of clique number that bounds treewidth throughout $\mathcal{G}$. **Cocks's conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{G}$ is $(\operatorname{tw},\omega)$-bounded if and only if $\mathcal{G}$ excludes a complete bipartite graph and, for every non-complete graph $H\in\mathcal{G}$, the class of all $H$-free graphs in $\mathcal{G}$ is $(\operatorname{tw},\omega)$-bounded. The source identifies this conjecture as still open and says that its pathwidth analogue follows from the paper's main theorem.
source_name: Sepehr Hajebi, “Polynomial bounds for pathwidth”, arXiv:2510.19120 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19120

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2025). “Chudnovsky and Trotignon refuted this conjecture in a strong sense, showing that neither polynomial nor any prescribed growth can be guaranteed in general.”
